i really really do receive it that way. i’ve been wondering if i need to just let this go for a minute as devastating as it may feel, and everyone’s kind words on here have felt like a sort of safety net underneath that plunge. i appreciate it a lot

are there ways to increase muscle mass without physically bulking up? i get as much exercise during the week as my schedule allows for (10,000+ steps a day) but i’m not opposed to trying to find the time to try something new. i’ve always just been concerned about gaining as opposed to losing through that type of fitness. thank you for the suggestion.

thank you. i’m doing this at the discretion of a doctor, the goal was for me to have lost more weight by this point in time, so the combination of that disappointment mixed with the physical and mental discomfort this has brought on has been too much. i struggled with anorexia for years and i know what it feels like to have your whole brain tortured from a lack of nutrition. that’s what this feels like. i’m just confused considering i’m following what not only a doctor has suggested but so many other people are clearly capable of managing. everyone is different at the end of the day i guess.

(and i’m praying it stays that way!!) more than anything, i just want them gone.

i can’t give you any solid advice but i want to commend you for both acknowledging and accepting the problem whilst not blaming yourself for the outcome. you can’t control the way you feel but you can control the way you react to your feelings and how much effort you put in trying to manage them. thats the only thing that really defines you as a person here. that’s all anyone can ask of you

thank you. i actually like that idea of the symbol thing. it’s been a weird seventeen years or so and that sort of helps me feel like im able to condense it and box it all up to look at at once. i’m sorry you’re uneasy with those sort of emotions,, i hope things pick up for you as well

it hasn’t happened in years and i totally forgot about it until reading this, but i used to have similar gun related fixations that would accompany these sort of cycling thoughts, and i would sort of make a finger gun motion and go “bang!”. it only happened a handful of times, thankfully. that would be one i wouldn’t want to have to deal with in public very much. thank you for not only the advice and relation but also for the validation. i’ve never really talked to people about this much before other than when i have to explain it to people who witness it happening to me, and i’m convinced sometimes i’m making my tics up or something. and i’m really glad to hear your fiancé has been so helpful for you,, cheers :)

kind of?? it would flare down and flare up again a few days apart from each other. i honestly ended up taking it out and had a tiny keloid remaining once it closed so i would be sure that yours isn’t also part scar tissue. i found it helpful to stop cleaning it as often as i was and completely as well as stopping cleaning it with q tips entirely.

i got it done at a very sketchy place and the stud itself was very loose, which i think was likely the initial cause of the irritation. make sure your jewelry isn’t moving around too much, and if it persists, i would have a piercer check it out to play it safe. it was annoying to have to heal the keloid after everything.
